title: He Sat in a Chair Next to a Fueled ICBM

scenes.voiceover: A Soviet Marshal had a chair carried out and sat down next to a fueled ICBM, to prove he wasn't afraid of it.
scenes.mainText: HE BROUGHT A CHAIR TO A FUELED ICBM
scenes.visualConcept: Nedelin memorial bust hard-lit, doom energy from frame one.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Nedelin memorial bust hard-lit, doom energy from frame one.

scenes.voiceover: October 1960. The missile was leaking. Draining it meant weeks of delay. Marshal Nedelin ordered it fixed. Live.
Dozens of engineers crawled over the loaded rocket like mechanics under a car.
Then the second stage ignited. Straight down. Into a fully fueled first stage.
scenes.visualConcept: Memorial obelisk against grey sky — the aftermath stands where the fire was.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Memorial obelisk against grey sky — the aftermath stands where the fire was.

scenes.voiceover: The official toll, admitted decades later: seventy eight dead. Other counts pass one hundred and twenty.
scenes.visualConcept: Count-up stat slam over memorial wall of names.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Count-up stat slam over memorial wall of names.

scenes.voiceover: The Marshal was identified by his melted medal. And Moscow told the world he died in a plane crash.
scenes.mainText: IDENTIFIED BY A MELTED MEDAL. "PLANE CRASH."
scenes.visualConcept: Nedelin bust again — the lie carved in granite.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Nedelin bust again — the lie carved in granite.

scenes.voiceover: It stayed secret for twenty nine years. And it was only erasure number one. The full story is on the channel.
scenes.mainText: THAT WAS ONLY No.1 → FULL STORY ON THE CHANNEL
scenes.visualConcept: Slow drift on the memorial, receding into dark.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: Slow drift on the memorial, receding into dark.
